items.title: The AI Safety Debate Has Lost the Plot. We Asked 10 Experts What the Real Nightmares Are | WIRED
items.summary: If AI is going to be one of the most significant advances in human civilization, then we should have an equally advanced political response. We should be making giant, no-regrets moves that give people and families economic resilience to withstand the changes. That is something that the richest nation on Earth at the richest moment in history, on the precipice of the greatest technological shift, can absolutely do. [...] I just think the issues presented by AI are so monstrously large, like: What is a person? What is writing? What is friendship? Would it be better to have artificial life forms than organic life forms? These are the monster questions that are typically the domain of the liberal arts, philosophy, and theology. There’s this strange new respect for it now. [...] Curiosity soon replaced my knee-jerk irritation. The summer of 2026 was a clear turning point in the AI narrative. items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet.

items.title: AI² Robotics Joins Indonesia’s National Strategic Industries | Gasgoo
items.summary:
Underpinning this deployment is AI² Robotics's integrated "Model × Hardware × Scenario" capability. The approach centers on a brain-like embodied large model as the intelligence core, mass-producible and stable robotic bodies as the vehicle, and real-world productivity scenarios as the driving force. [...] Gasgoo Munich-On November 9, AI² Robotics announced it has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Danantara Development Management Fund (DDMF), the investment arm of Indonesia's state-backed wealth fund Danantara Indonesia. The partnership will focus on pilot applications, industrial collaboration, and local deployment of general-purpose intelligent robots and embodied AI technology across the archipelago. [...] The agreement was signed during the inaugural Danantara Technology Innovation Investment Forum (DTIIF 2026) in Jakarta, with Zhang Peng, AI² Robotics's co-founder, signing on behalf of the company.

Image Credit: AI² Robotics

Operating independently under the president's office, Danantara Indonesia holds substantial influence. AI² Robotics is now the first—and currently the only—robotics company to join DDMF's embodied AI cooperation roster.

items.title: Promise Robotics partners with D.R. Horton on physical AI for homebuilding - The Robot Report
items.summary: Promise Robotics said its technology interprets existing home designs, generates production plans and robotic instructions, orchestrates manufacturing, and connects that production with site installation. Rather than automating isolated tasks, the company said it brings these capabilities together in one integrated environment. [...] Promise Robotics is not a vertically integrated developer or a home designer like Reframe Systems, Attar acknowledged. “We’re more about the advancements in robotics, and we’re here to scale when companies need to scale,” he said. [...] “At D.R. Horton, we are always looking for innovations that can help us improve how we build. We are continuously focused on improving cycle times, increasing production capacity, and bringing greater consistency and predictability to our operations,” said Brad Conlon, senior vice president for strategic growth and innovation at D.R. Horton. “Promise Robotics’ integrated platform gives us a new capability to support those goals.”
